## Known biases

PLUTO describes tax lots, not buildings. On a lot with several buildings, the building class, units, floor area and basement code are those of the lot, and NumFloors is that of the tallest building on the lot (data dictionary, NumFloors); the lab uses NumFloors directly only where the lot has one building, and flags it on the lot&\#x27;s largest footprint otherwise (rule A-4). The fields come from the Department of Finance&\#x27;s tax and appraisal systems (PTS, CAMA): building class is an assessment class, not a survey of use; BsmtCode is stated to be available for one, two or three family structures and not verified by DOF for other property; a zero floor area or empty NumFloors on a lot with buildings means not available. A condominium is one billing lot (75xx) holding the classes of its unit lots merged by DCP (RC, RD, RM, RX, RZ, RI). The table is the city as of the 26v3 release (November 2026), not as of a storm date. Of the 17,195 lots asked, 15,590 were returned: the others are mainly base\_bbl values of condominium unit lots, which PLUTO does not hold as rows (the lab joins on mappluto\_bbl first). AssessTot is a tax assessment, not a replacement value, and is not used.
